prompt: Simplify: $x^3 \cdot x^4$. Write your answer as a power of $x$.
hint: Each power is a string of copies of $x$ being multiplied. Think about how many copies there are altogether.

hints.text: Each power is a string of copies of $x$ being multiplied. Think about how many copies there are altogether.
$x^3$ has $3$ copies and $x^4$ has $4$ more, so multiplying powers of the same base adds the exponents: $x^{3+4}$.

explanation: Write out the copies of $x$ in each power: $x^3 \cdot x^4$ means $(x \cdot x \cdot x)(x \cdot x \cdot x \cdot x)$.
Count the factors of $x$ in the whole product: $3 + 4 = 7$ copies.
So $x^3 \cdot x^4 = x^7$. This is the product rule: add the exponents when the bases match.

alternativeExplanations.title: Test with real numbers
steps: 128 is 2⁷, not 2¹². So the exponents add: x⁷.

alternativeExplanations.title: Two boxes of copies
steps: Picture a box holding 3 x-tiles and a box holding 4 x-tiles, all being multiplied together.
Dump both boxes into one: 3 + 4 = 7 tiles, which is x⁷.
